title: Seller value-thread stitch deck (pilot scripts + tech vignettes) - iter0
content:
Slide 1: Purpose & how to use this deck
- One-sheet for SEs and AMs to stitch product capabilities into a buyer's value-thread.
- Not a product spec; a playbook for quick pilot scoping and surfacing technical risks that matter to buyers.
Speaker notes: Use this at the end of a discovery to propose a 4-week pilot. Emphasize the economics and fallback story early.

Slide 2: What is a value-thread stitch?
- Value-thread = concrete buyer outcome + the runtime levers that deliver it (latency, cost, quality, reliability).
- Stitch = map Redwood features to the buyer's thread (e.g., cache for prefix reuse, dedicated for throughput, routing for cost/latency balance).
- Outcome: helps technical buyers see direct tradeoffs and procurement see predictable costs.
Speaker notes: This framing short-circuits fuzzy conversations. Show one micro-example in the discovery.

Slide 3: Persona matrix (one-liners)
- Integration Architect: cares about latency tail, deterministic routing, on-call complexity.
- Platform Engineer: capacity planning, autoscale, dedicated pools, security controls.
- Product PM (revenue): latency impact on conversion and model quality drift.
- CFO/Procurement: predictable unit cost, reserved capacity discounts, SLA exposure.
Speaker notes: Call out who to invite to the pilot kickoff. If Procurement is in, push dedicated or committed capacity options.

Slide 4: Micro-evidence cards (copyable bites for customer decks)
- "Prefix/KV caching reduced per-token cost by >40% on retrieval-heavy flows."
- "Redwood routing cut 95th percentile latency by 30ms through region-aware fallback."
- "Dedicated pools delivered linear throughput scaling for 2x concurrent streamers in production."
Speaker notes: Keep these short; cite internal benchmarks if asked (link INF-ONRAMP-125).

Slide 5: Pilot offer (4-week, low-friction)
- Week 0: Kickoff + success metrics alignment + baseline token/latency profile capture.
- Week 1-2: Implement routing + cache + one quantization profile for cost test.
- Week 3: Run load/latency validation + regression checks + sample evals.
- Week 4: Hand-off + runbook + 1-week monitoring window for acceptance.
Speaker notes: Sell the short timebox and clear exit criteria. Keep it focused: one endpoint, one model family.

Slide 6: Pilot success metrics (example set)
- Latency: 95th percentile < buyer target (e.g., 300ms) for interactive flows.
- Cost: % cost reduction vs baseline (target 20–40% depending on cacheability).
- Quality: automated eval pass rate >= 98% on curated prompt set.
- Reliability: error rate < 0.5% and graceful fallback in 100% of simulated region loss tests.
Speaker notes: Agree these during kickoff. If buyer only care about cost, stretch on latency.

Slide 7: Technical vignettes (bring these as mini-stories)
- Vignette A: Customer had 60% repeated prompts; caching reduced tokens and costs, retained quality.
  - Hook: show token-count waterfall pre/post.
- Vignette B: Multi-region retail app needed <200ms p95; we used region routing + model variant fallback to meet SLO.
  - Hook: show routing policy and fallback story.
- Vignette C: Risk-averse enterprise needed air-gapped telemetry + KMS; we used Private deployment and audit logs.
  - Hook: compliance checklist + time-to-deploy estimate.
Speaker notes: Keep a short artifact (2–3 slides) for each vignette to share in follow-ups.

Slide 8: Objections & micro-responses (engineer-friendly)
- "We can't risk model regressions." -> "We run evals on your prompt set pre/post; flag regressions and autopromote fallback variants until resolved."
- "Cost unpredictable with pay-as-you-go." -> "Reserve a small Dedicated pool for pilot or set per-route quotas + cost alerts."
- "Latency tails annoy us." -> "Use region routing + KV cache + shed non-critical traffic to lower tiers; we'll simulate in Week 2."
Speaker notes: Teach SEs to repeat the customer's language: 'regressions', 'tails', 'predictability'.

Slide 9: Quick demo script (3-minute technical walkthrough)
- Start: Show baseline call (100ms cold, 450ms p95).
- Flip on cache: show token reduction and 40% latency improvement.
- Route to dedicated: show throughput increase under concurrency.
- Toggle fallback: simulate region loss and show consistent degradation to fallback model instead of hard failure.
Speaker notes: Practice transitions. Keep demo deterministic — use recorded traffic or small seed data.

Slide 10: CFO-facing ROI micro-calculator (copyable template)
- Inputs: baseline tokens/day (T), baseline token cost ($0.0003/token*), expected cacheable fraction (C), expected latency-related revenue boost (R%).
- Simple calc: projected token cost = T * (1 - C) * $unit + infra premiums (reserved discount).
- Example: T=1,000,000 tokens/day, C=0.35 -> saved 350k tokens/day -> $105/day saved at $0.0003/token.
- Note: Include engineering uplift costs and reserved discounts in final ARR math.
Speaker notes: Make this into a shared spreadsheet linked in follow-up emails.

Slide 11: Canary + rollback mini-checklist (for SEs running pilot)
- Pre-canary: collect baseline traces, secure keys, enable debug logs.
- Canary run: 5% traffic for 24 hours; monitor p50/p95, error rates, and eval pass rate.
- Rollback triggers: eval regression > 2% absolute, error spike > 2x baseline, or latency breach > 2x SLO.
- Post-canary: summary and recommend next steps (scale/commit/abort).
Speaker notes: Keep checklist pinned in the pilot ticket; include responsible owners and Slack escalation channel.

Slide 12: Follow-up assets & next steps (what to send right after demo)
- One-pager: value-thread map + pilot plan + CFO ROI snippet.
- Tech appendix: sample config snippets (routing JSON, cache ttl guidance).
- Eval kit: templated prompts + assert rules + script to compute pass rate.
- Ask: 2-week calendar slot for kickoff, primary dev contact, security contact.
Speaker notes: Attach linked artifacts (INF-ONRAMP-125) and our short FAQ.

Slide 13: Open questions (internal)
- Need an up-to-date cost-per-token number per model variant for field math.
- Who owns the pilot runbook template in the console docs?
- Can SRE pre-create a small dedicated pool for pilots (<$X/month)?
TODO: assign owners in next GTM weekly.

Slide 14: Appendix: copy-and-paste rebuttal snippets
- For SEs: "We start with a single endpoint and your prompt set; we measure regressions before any rollouts and keep a live fallback until you're comfortable."
- For CFO: "We provide committed options so you can cap monthly spend; pilots often show predictable unit economics within 4 weeks."
- For Architects: "We'll provide a region-aware routing policy and a test harness to simulate regional outage scenarios."
